name: Tata Communications

profile.address: 8343, Northeast Evergreen Parkway, Tanasbourne, Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon, 97124
profile.reading: This Tata Communications facility sits on Northeast Evergreen Parkway in the Tanasbourne area of Hillsboro, Oregon, part of the Portland metro corridor known for chip manufacturing and telecommunications infrastructure. It carries the TGN designation, an abbreviation for the Tata Global Network, the name Tata Communications uses for the wholly owned undersea and terrestrial fiber system it built up around assets originally developed by Tyco Telecommunications. Hillsboro is not a coastal town, so this address most likely functions as an inland cable landing or terminating facility of the kind carriers use to bring a subsea cable's terminated fiber into a secure, road accessible building away from the immediate shoreline, before handing it off into terrestrial backhaul networks reaching Portland and beyond. As with Tata's other cable landing infrastructure, the company does not publish square footage, power capacity, or tenancy information for this specific site. That is consistent with how the submarine cable industry treats individual landing and terminating stations, which are typically described only in aggregate cable system documentation rather than as standalone real estate assets. No county permit or building record specific to this address was found in the course of this research. The facility should be understood as working carrier infrastructure supporting Tata's Pacific network reach, rather than a commercial, multi tenant data center.

reading:
Tata Communications is a global network carrier headquartered in Mumbai and part of the Tata Group. It owns and operates one of the largest wholly owned subsea cable networks in the world, marketed as the Tata Global Network, and its presence in this registry is a cable landing station rather than a data centre in the ordinary sense.

The single United States facility recorded here is the TGN Hillsboro station in Washington County, Oregon, mapped as a private industrial building about 11.7 metres tall on Evergreen Parkway. The address is worth walking through, because two different addresses circulate for the same building and the city resolved the confusion itself. Published cable station references give the station as 21101 Northwest Evergreen Parkway. The registry's mapped record gives 8343 Northeast Evergreen Parkway. Under Phase 3-F of the Connecting Hillsboro Address Project, dated 26 March 2018, the City of Hillsboro reassigned 21101 NW Evergreen Parkway to 8343 NE Evergreen Parkway, with both valid for postal mail during a transition and the new address required in full use for non residential sites by 31 March 2020. They are the same building, and the discrepancy is a municipal readdressing, not two facilities.

The station terminates TGN Pacific, the trans Pacific segment Tata describes as roughly 22,300 kilometres between the United States and Japan, with Japanese landings at Emi and at Toyohashi in Aichi Prefecture. The wet plant comes ashore on the Oregon coast at Nedonna Beach and Rockaway Beach, about 150 miles away, and is backhauled inland to Hillsboro. The station was originally built and operated by Tyco Telecommunications and passed to VSNL when VSNL acquired the Tyco Global Network in 2005, VSNL later being rebranded Tata Communications. In January 2014 Tata announced a 100 gigabit per second upgrade across TGN Pacific using Ciena's 6500 platform and GeoMesh, alongside about 6,700 kilometres of TGN Intra-Asia routes. Hillsboro holds three cable landing stations within roughly a mile of each other, the TGN station alongside the Southern Cross and Trans-Pacific Express stations, which is why the city functions as a Pacific landing hub.

No power figure of any kind has been published for the building. A landing station's demand is dominated by power feeding equipment for the submarine repeaters and by backhaul transmission gear rather than by racks of general purpose compute, and the 22,300 kilometre and 100 gigabit figures are optical, not electrical. This registry stores no capacity here.

One corporate distinction avoids a common error. The branded colocation business that once carried the Tata Communications name moved to ST Telemedia Global Data Centres in 2021, when STT GDC acquired Tata's remaining stake in their Singapore joint venture. The subsea network and its United States landing stations were not part of that transaction. A separate registry record named simply Tata, tied to the Wall Township landing station in New Jersey where Tata leases carrier neutral meet me room space to NJFX, is the same company and is linked by duplicate_of rather than merged.
